key_insight: RaDaR is a compact open-source reasoning LLM designed for rare disease diagnosis that outperformed other evaluated open models and improved physician diagnostic accuracy in a randomized assistance trial.
clinical_relevance: The model may help clinicians reach rare disease diagnoses earlier, potentially shortening the long diagnostic delay common in low-prevalence conditions.
method: Trained on 49,170 public free-text cases plus 104,666 synthetic reasoning-enhanced cases
Evaluated against public benchmarks and four external validation centers
Tested in a retrospective cohort and a randomized physician-assistance trial
evidence_signal: In retrospective analysis, RaDaR prioritized the final diagnosis before documented clinical suspicion in 61.06% of cases, and physician assistance improved rare-disease diagnostic accuracy by 21.44 percentage points versus internet search alone.
watch_item: Results are promising but depend on high-quality integration, external validation, and careful oversight because performance may vary across institutions and rare-disease case mixes.
paper_title: A specialized reasoning large language model for accelerating rare disease diagnosis: a randomized AI physician assistance trial
